# NetworkDNS

`c.NetworkDNS` calls the API's NetworkDNS group. The DNS resolvers of each
interface of the host.

| Method                                            | Returns                                   | Permission  | Description                                       |
| ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| [`Get(ctx, hostname, interfaceName)`](#get)       | `*Response[Collection[NetworkDnsEntry]]`  | `dns:read`  | Get the DNS resolvers of an interface.            |
| [`Update(ctx, hostname, input)`](#update)         | `*Response[Collection[NetworkDnsResult]]` | `dns:write` | Set the DNS resolvers of an interface.            |
| [`Delete(ctx, hostname, interfaceName)`](#delete) | `*Response[Collection[NetworkDnsResult]]` | `dns:write` | Drop the DNS resolvers osapi set on an interface. |

### Get

```go
func (s *NetworkDNSService) Get(
	ctx context.Context,
	hostname string,
	interfaceName string,
) (*Response[Collection[NetworkDnsEntry]], error)
```

Get the DNS resolvers of an interface.

Reads the servers and the search domains of the interface: resolvectl on Linux,
with resolv.conf on a host that has no resolvers per interface, such as a
container, and scutil on macOS.

It sends `GET /api/node/{hostname}/network/dns/{interface_name}`, and needs the
permission `dns:read`.

The examples of the method's definition:

An interface with servers and a domain, `go run network_dns.go get`:

```go
resp, err := c.NetworkDNS.Get(ctx, target, "osapi0")
```

A Mac, `go run network_dns.go get-2`:

```go
resp, err := c.NetworkDNS.Get(ctx, target, "en0")
```

### Update

```go
func (s *NetworkDNSService) Update(
	ctx context.Context,
	hostname string,
	input NetworkDNSUpdateInput,
) (*Response[Collection[NetworkDnsResult]], error)
```

Set the DNS resolvers of an interface.

Writes a netplan file of the interface's own, such as
/etc/netplan/osapi-dns-eth0.yaml for eth0, under the netplan definition that
matches the interface, and applies it. A definition that matches several
interfaces, such as cloud-init's all for en*, gives each of them the resolvers.
An empty list keeps the interface's servers or domains, and an interface with no
resolvers yet starts from none. override_dhcp drops the servers DHCP gives. It
runs on the Debian family, and elsewhere, and in a container, reports skipped.

It sends `PUT /api/node/{hostname}/network/dns/{interface_name}`, and needs the
permission `dns:write`.

The examples of the method's definition:

Set the servers of an interface, `go run network_dns.go update`:

```go
resp, err := c.NetworkDNS.Update(ctx, target, client.NetworkDNSUpdateInput{
	InterfaceName: "osapi0",
	Servers:       []string{"9.9.9.9"},
})
```

Set the search domains, and keep the servers, `go run network_dns.go update-2`:

```go
resp, err := c.NetworkDNS.Update(ctx, target, client.NetworkDNSUpdateInput{
	InterfaceName: "osapi0",
	OverrideDHCP:  true,
	SearchDomains: []string{"corp.example"},
})
```

### Delete

```go
func (s *NetworkDNSService) Delete(
	ctx context.Context,
	hostname string,
	interfaceName string,
) (*Response[Collection[NetworkDnsResult]], error)
```

Drop the DNS resolvers osapi set on an interface.

Removes the interface's netplan file and applies what is left. An interface
osapi set nothing on does not change.

It sends `DELETE /api/node/{hostname}/network/dns/{interface_name}`, and needs
the permission `dns:write`.

The examples of the method's definition:

An interface osapi set, `go run network_dns.go delete`:

```go
resp, err := c.NetworkDNS.Delete(ctx, target, "osapi0")
```
